newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA NAPHTHA/MOGAS - TAIWAN TENDER RESULT SUPPORTIVE.
newsitem.headline: ASIA NAPHTHA/MOGAS - TAIWAN TENDER RESULT SUPPORTIVE.

text.p: Taiwan's award of three reformate cargoes for September delivery supported gasoline prices on Wednesday despite the drop in crude.
"It should take away some length...the market for September was long," said a trader with a major oil company.
"The market looks healthier," another commented on the results. "At least it awarded three cargoes -- from Singapore, Thailand and South Korea."

After long-drawn negotiations, Taiwan state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) bought by tender late Wednesday, three 250,000-barrel cargoes of 95-octane unleaded reformate from different sellers at $24.19 per barrel, c-and-f, a CPC official said.
"They were all awarded at the same price...from different sellers," he said.
Two of the sellers, a Japanese trader and a U.S. major confirmed the award but said it was awarded at $24.30 and higher.
The third possible seller, another U.S. major said it had not received any confirmation as yet.
Although the tender closed August 11 and was valid for two days, CPC spent longer than the usual one day to it takes to deliberate the offers.

After the close of the tender, CPC officials told Reuters it had received nine offers over $24.00 per barrel in its 95-octane unleaded reformate import tender for September, and would try to counter offer at $24.10 or $24.20.
The official said no further September tenders will be issued as the award was "enough for the month."
Taiwan which usually buys one to two cargoes every half-month, took the large volume after it cancelled an earlier tender for the for first half of September due to high offers over $25.30.
"It seems like the sellers lowered than their original offers, and at least the price is lower than the $25 that was cancelled," said a trader.
Traders said this is also the first time CPC has paid a premium over the published Singapore quote and freight.
Singapore September naphtha swaps fell after trading at $21.40 per barrel with weaker crude, and was last quoted at $21.30/$21.40.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
